blocks.text: Rad Dog, also known as Neon Surf Shack, is a design aesthetic (often diffused with "Rad Dog" and "Neon Ooze") prevalent between the late 1980s and early 1990s movement. It centers on radical skate imagery, loud neon colors, tribal motifs, surf graphics, and a mix of retro 1950s–1960s indigenous or tiki Hawaiian art. Its main focus of the aesthetic incorporates hypercolors, lime green, electric blue, hot pink, vibrant yellow splatters, tropical geometric shapes, hand drawn line work, sludge/ooze accents, and energetic typography. Sometimes it can appear in edgy, youth-marketed surf, skate and snowboarding gear from vintage brands like Billabong or early Stüssy.
Surf and Skate Culture: Sun-faded hats, bold t-shirts, geometric patterns, and cartoon sharks.
Slime / Ooze Elements: Toxic waste green, weird blobs, and gross-out cartoon art that was prominent in teens' and kids' media back then.
Bright neon Colors: Greens, day-glow pinks, and blues pop against light or dark backgrounds.
